agent_note: Which AI runs the jobs: claude (Claude Code, the default), grok (Grok CLI) or codex (OpenAI's Codex CLI, signed in with a ChatGPT account; Gmail and Slack come from that account's ChatGPT connectors, and Miro is not available). model / effort are Claude's; codex_model / codex_effort are Codex's (blank = Codex's built-in default; Open Loops never uses your own Codex settings), codex_timeout_s how long one Codex run may take. Grok takes neither.

auto_chase.note: When enabled, the morning run chases any waiting loop quiet for after_workdays (from the ask or the last chase), up to max_chases times. Each card has an 'auto: on/off' switch. Draft vs send follows send_internal / send_external.

tone.base: Warm, friendly British English. Sounds like a colleague who likes the person, not a ticketing system. Never passive-aggressive, never counts how many times you've asked. Assumes they're busy, makes it easy to answer (one clear question, offers to hop on a call or do the legwork). Short: 2-4 sentences. Ends on a light note.
tone.senior: Respectful and relaxed. Frame it as keeping them in the loop and asking for a steer and managing up, not chasing. 'When you get a sec' / 'no rush if it's this week'. Give the one-line reason it matters. Sign off warmly.
tone.peer: Casual and direct, first names, a bit of humour is fine. Ask straight, offer help.
tone.junior: Encouraging and clear. Say exactly what you need and by when, thank them, make it obvious it's fine to ask questions.
tone.external: Polite, professional but human. Reference the thread, one specific ask, a soft deadline, thanks for their time.

escalation.1: first nudge - light touch, friendly check-in
escalation.2: second - still warm, add a concrete date or what it unblocks, offer a quick call
escalation.3: third+ - kind but clear that it's now blocking; ask for a yes/no or who else can help. Still no counting of previous asks.

send_note: send_internal / send_external: when ticked, chases to that group are SENT immediately (Slack message / Gmail reply) instead of drafted. Internal = email domain in internal_domains (or a Slack contact with no email). External = anyone else, e.g. vendors and agencies.
